Thermal barrier and environmental barrier coatings (TBCs and EBCs) have been developed to protect metallic and Si-based ceramic components in gas turbine engines from high temperature attack.
Zirconia-yttria based oxides and (Ba,Sr)Al2Si2O8 (BSAS)/mullite based silicates have been used as the coating materials.

The thermal conductivity was measured using a steady-state laser heat flux technique, where the specimen surface was heated by a high power laser and the temperature gradient across the specimen was measured using pyrometers.
The hot-pressed zirconia-yttria coatings had thermal conductivity values of 2.0 to 2.3 W/m-K.
The plasma-sprayed zirconia-yttria coatings had initial values of 1.0 W/m-K which increased to 1.4 W/m-K after 20 hours of high temperature exposure due to sintering.
The hot-pressed BSAS coatings had thermal conductivity values of 2.8 to 3.0 W/m-K.
The plasma-sprayed mullite coatings showed thermal conductivity values of 1.9 to 2.5 W/m-K in the 1000 to 1400°C range.
The hot-pressed BSAS and mullite mixture coatings had thermal conductivity values of about 3.0 W/m-K at 600°C and 1.6 to 2.0 W/m-K at 1500°C.
The plasma-sprayed coatings showed lower initial conductivity values (1.4 W/m-K for EBCs and 1.0 W/m-K for ZrO2-8wt%Y2O3) compared to the hot-pressed bulk materials due to their higher porosity.
Significant increases in thermal conductivity were observed for the plasma-sprayed TBC and EBC coating systems after high temperature laser exposure, due to ceramic sintering and densification.
For a ZrO2-8wt%Y2O3/mullite/Si/SiC-SiC CMC system, the initial overall ceramic coating conductivity was 1.6-1.8 W/m-K, but quickly increased to about 2.2 W/m-K after high temperature exposure.
The higher BSAS containing BSAS and mullite mixture coatings showed slightly higher thermal conductivity compared to the lower BSAS containing mixtures.
The plasma-sprayed BSAS coatings showed an initial conductivity of 1.4 W/m-K at 900°C, which increased to ~2.2 W/m-K after the first heating-cooling cycle due to sintering.
The plasma-sprayed BSAS+mullite mixture coatings showed less conductivity increase due to sintering compared to the pure BSAS coatings.

The thermal conductivity of the multilayer TBC/EBC coatings increased quickly during the first high temperature exposure due to sintering and densification, but showed much less increase in the subsequent cycles.
